Can a squatter take title to a Virginia house?

Only after a long period, and the statute sets a time limit rather than a simple recipe. Virginia law bars anyone from entering or suing to recover land unless it is done within fifteen years after the right first accrued to that person or to someone through whom he claims (Va. Code 8.01-236). That limitation is the rule underneath adverse possession: once an owner's right to recover has expired, a person in long possession can argue the owner is out of time.

The statutes we read do not list the elements a court weighs, so the details of a claim, such as what kind of possession counts, come from court decisions. A Virginia attorney can tell you how those decisions apply to a particular property.

The clock also has a ceiling for owners with a legal disability. No disability, and no adding together of disabilities, preserves a right to enter or sue for more than twenty-five years after it first accrued, even if the person was disabled the entire time (Va. Code 8.01-237).

Why does a vacant or inherited house raise the issue?

A house that nobody checks on is the easiest place for an unwelcome occupant to settle in. Heirs who live out of state, owners in a nursing home, and estates waiting for probate all leave properties empty for months. Virginia has 95 counties and 38 independent cities, with Fairfax County the largest jurisdiction and more than one-third of residents in Northern Virginia, so a vacant house can be anywhere from a dense suburb to a rural mountain parcel (Wikipedia, Virginia).

Practical steps that cost little:

  • Post clear no trespassing signs and tell the occupant in writing to leave.
  • Keep dated photos and records of who has keys, utilities and mail.
  • Pay property tax on time so the property does not also face a delinquency suit.
  • Visit on a schedule, or ask a neighbor or property manager to do so.

What can an owner do about an unlawful occupant?

The statutes give an owner two court routes. The first is a motion for judgment in circuit court when someone makes a forcible or unlawful entry on land, or a tenant keeps possession after the right has expired (Va. Code 8.01-124). The action must be brought within three years after the entry or detainer.

The second is a summons for unlawful detainer. The owner presents a sworn statement of the facts to a magistrate, or to a clerk or judge of a general district court, who issues the summons. It must be served at least 10 days before the return day (Va. Code 8.01-126).

The statute also has a faster track for single-family homes. If the owner of a residential single family dwelling files, and the court finds all three of the following, an emergency hearing is held as soon as practicable and within 14 days of filing, or at the latest within 30 days:

  • no rental agreement exists or ever existed between the owner and the occupant;
  • the occupant lives there without the owner's permission;
  • the owner gave the occupant written notice to vacate at least 72 hours before filing.

The text of this section has more than one version with different effective dates, so confirm the current wording with the court clerk before you file.

What does the court case look like step by step?

The table summarizes what the statutes say about the main stages of an unlawful detainer.

StageWhat the statute provides
NoticeWritten notice to vacate at least 72 hours before filing, for the emergency single family hearing
SummonsIssued on the owner's sworn statement; served at least 10 days before the return day
HearingEmergency hearing within 14 days of filing when the conditions are met, otherwise within 30 days at the latest
JudgmentJudgment for the premises, plus proven damages and rent owed; possession can be ordered at the first hearing
AppealWithin 10 days, with bond posted and writ tax paid within 10 days
EvictionSheriff serves notice at least 72 hours before executing the writ, and not before the 10-day appeal period ends

At the initial hearing the plaintiff can receive a final, appealable judgment for possession and an order of possession. On request, the court can split the case and set a later date, no more than 120 days out, to fix final rent and damages (Va. Code 8.01-128). If the owner wins, the judge can order the writ of eviction to issue immediately on request. An indigent defendant does not need to post an appeal bond (Va. Code 8.01-129).

Is staying on the property after being told to leave a crime?

It can be. A person who goes onto or stays on another's land, buildings or premises after being forbidden to do so, orally, in writing or by a posted sign, is guilty of a Class 1 misdemeanor (Va. Code 18.2-119). The statute applies to the owner, lessee, custodian or their agent who gave the warning.

A criminal charge is separate from the civil case that decides possession. The court process above is how possession is decided.

What if the occupant is a former owner after a foreclosure?

A former owner still in a single-family home on the day of a foreclosure sale becomes a tenant at sufferance. The successor owner can end that tenancy with a written termination notice given at least three days before the termination date, then file an unlawful detainer. The former owner owes fair market rent from the date of the foreclosure until leaving, plus damages, reasonable attorney fees and court costs (Va. Code 8.01-126).

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Virginia houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How does an occupant problem affect selling the house?

It affects price, timing and who will buy. A buyer who needs a loan will generally need the home empty and inspectable, and an open court case can delay that. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can sometimes take the property with the occupant issue still pending, so ask the buyer whether they will do that and who handles the legal filing.

Keep in mind that the seller remains responsible for taxes until closing. If the house is behind on tax, the lien ranks ahead of other liens, and a long delinquency can lead to a judicial sale, so a tax payoff may be part of the same closing.

Before choosing a path, write down every fact about how the person got in: any lease, any text or email permission, the dates and what you have done to demand that they leave. A short consultation with a Virginia attorney can tell you whether to file for unlawful detainer first or negotiate a move-out date.

More questions about Virginia Squatters Rights and Adverse Possession

How many years does adverse possession take in Virginia?

The statute cited for the underlying limitation is fifteen years from when an owner's right to enter or sue first accrued. Court decisions decide what a claimant must prove, so talk to a Virginia attorney about specific facts.

Can I change the locks and remove a squatter myself?

Do not rely on that. The statutes give owners court routes, a motion for judgment in circuit court or a summons for unlawful detainer, and an eviction is carried out by the sheriff under a writ. Ask an attorney before taking any step yourself.

How fast can an unlawful detainer be heard?

For a single-family home with no rental agreement, no permission and a 72 hour written notice, an emergency hearing is set within 14 days of filing, or at the latest within 30 days.

What if the occupant appeals?

An appeal to circuit court must be taken within 10 days, with bond and the writ tax paid within that time, and the sheriff cannot evict before the 10-day period ends. Indigent defendants are not required to post a bond.

Is trespass a crime in Virginia?

Staying after being forbidden to remain, orally, in writing or by posted sign, is a Class 1 misdemeanor under Va. Code 18.2-119.

Can I sell a house that has an unwelcome occupant?

Yes, but expect the occupant to affect buyers and timing. As-is buyers may accept that risk, and your closing agent will need a clear plan for possession.

title: Virginia Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights: Rules for Selling a Rental

Virginia Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights: Rules for Selling a Rental

  • Turn the Virginia Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Virginia House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Virginia?
We buy Virginia houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

What paperwork must a Virginia landlord give a new tenant?

A landlord must offer a written rental agreement and hand over the statement of tenant rights and responsibilities from the Department of Housing and Community Development. That duty is in Va. Code 55.1-1204.

Both sides sign an acknowledgment form showing the tenant received the statement. If the tenant will not sign, the landlord records the date or dates the form was provided and that the tenant did not sign. The landlord then gives the tenant a copy of the signed agreement and the statement within 10 business days of the effective date.

Missing that delivery does not void the lease. It does stop the landlord from filing or keeping any action, including an unlawful detainer, for an alleged lease violation until the tenant has received the statement. For an owner selling a rented house, a missing acknowledgment is the first thing to look for in the file.

What if there is no written lease?

If the landlord never offers a written agreement, the same section creates a tenancy by operation of law with fixed terms. A buyer or seller who finds an oral arrangement should know these defaults.

  • The chapter applies to the unit, and the term is 12 months with no automatic renewal, except for month-to-month cases.
  • Rent is paid in 12 equal installments at an agreed amount, or at fair market rent if none was agreed.
  • Rent is due the first of the month and counts as late after the fifth.
  • The landlord may collect a deposit of up to two months of rent.
  • The parties may sign a written agreement at any time during the 12 months.

Where a rent period is weekly, the tenancy is week-to-week. In all other cases it is month-to-month unless the agreement says otherwise.

How much can a landlord charge for late rent and payment fees?

A late charge is allowed only if the written agreement provides for it, and it cannot exceed the lesser of 10 percent of the periodic rent or 10 percent of the balance due.

A landlord must accept rent and deposit by check and money order, and give a written receipt for cash or money order payments. Collection or processing fees are barred unless an alternative with no extra fee is offered. Where a fee is charged, it cannot exceed the actual out-of-pocket cost billed by a third party for the card or electronic payment. Landlords with four or fewer rental units are not required to accept debit or credit cards.

A tenant can ask in writing for a statement of charges and payments, and the landlord must provide it within 10 business days, covering the tenancy or the past 12 months, whichever is shorter.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Virginia house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What extra rules apply to landlords with more than four rentals?

Landlords who own more than four rental units, or more than a 10 percent interest in more than four, must follow added notice rules for renewals. Those rules sit in subsection K of 55.1-1204 and are summarized below.

RuleVersion now in forceVersion effective July 1, 2027
Rent increase noticeWritten notice at least 60 days before the term endsWritten notice at least 90 days before the term ends, with a reply deadline at least 30 days after delivery
Nonrenewal noticeAt least 60 days before the term endsAt least 60 days before the term ends
Payment plan for small rent balancesNot requiredRequired before the 14-day rent notice in certain cases (55.1-1245)

Neither notice rule applies to a periodic tenancy created by operation of law under subsection C of 55.1-1253. If you rent out one house, these provisions probably do not reach you, but a portfolio owner selling several houses should treat them as live.

How does the security deposit work?

A Virginia landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit above two months of periodic rent, and must itemize any deductions in writing within 45 days after the tenancy ends or the tenant leaves, whichever is last. The rules are in Va. Code 55.1-1226.

  • Deductions are limited to accrued rent and late charges, damage beyond reasonable wear and tear, other charges in the lease, and actual damages for breach.
  • With more than one tenant, the refund is one check payable to all of them, unless they agreed otherwise in writing.
  • If no forwarding address is given, the landlord may hold the money, and after one year past the 45 days may send it to the State Treasurer as unclaimed property.
  • A landlord may withhold a reasonable part for unpaid water, sewer or other utility bills if prior written notice was given; a tenant who proves payment gets the money back.
  • Records of deductions must be kept for two years and be open to the tenant during business hours.
  • A tenant may be offered damage insurance in place of a deposit if it meets the listed criteria.

Tenants can ask to be present at the move-out inspection, which must happen within 72 hours of delivering possession. If the landlord willfully fails to comply, the court orders the deposit returned along with actual damages and reasonable attorney fees, unless the tenant owes rent, in which case the deposit is credited against that rent.

What happens to the deposit when the rental is sold?

The person who holds the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends is bound by the deposit statute and must return any deposit that is duly owed. That is true however the interest was acquired, whether or not the deposit was transferred, and regardless of any contract between the old and new owners.

For a seller, the practical steps are simple.

  • List every deposit held and who paid it.
  • Collect the itemized deduction records for the last two years.
  • Ask the buyer to agree in writing how deposits will be credited at closing, and confirm the tenant is told.
  • Keep the signed rights acknowledgment and the lease together for the buyer.

These steps are suggestions for organizing the file. They are not legal advice, and an attorney should review the closing paperwork.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Virginia houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What remedies does a landlord have after ending the lease?

Once the lease is terminated, 55.1-1251 gives the landlord a claim for possession and rent, plus a separate claim for actual damages, attorney fees and service costs. Damages can include rent through the end of the term or the start of a new tenancy, but the landlord must mitigate and cannot seek accelerated rent in a post-possession judgment.

When a tenant moves out by choice or by writ, the deposit is credited following the 45-day rule above.

More questions about Virginia Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights

What is the maximum security deposit in Virginia?

Two months of periodic rent. The landlord must itemize deductions and return the balance within 45 days after the tenancy ends or the tenant leaves, whichever is last.

Can a landlord charge any late fee in Virginia?

Only if the written lease provides for it, and the charge cannot exceed the lesser of 10 percent of the periodic rent or 10 percent of the balance owed.

Does a missing tenant rights form void a lease?

No. The lease stays valid, but the landlord cannot file or maintain an unlawful detainer for an alleged lease violation until the tenant has the statement of rights and responsibilities.

What are the default terms if there is no written lease?

A 12-month tenancy with no automatic renewal, rent due on the first and late after the fifth, and a deposit of up to two months of rent. A weekly payer is week-to-week.

Who must return the tenant's deposit after a sale?

The holder of the landlord's interest when the tenancy ends. That holder is bound even if the deposit did not transfer with the property.

Do larger landlords have extra duties?

Yes. Owners of more than four rental units must give written notice of rent increases and nonrenewal at least 60 days before the term ends, and the rules shift on July 1, 2027, to a 90-day notice for increases.

title: Virginia Eviction Notice Rules: Notice Types, Days and Selling the House
content:
Virginia Eviction Notice Rules: Notice Types, Days and Selling the House

Cash Home Buyers in Virginia
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Virginia Eviction Notice Rules: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Virginia Eviction Notice Rules sale
  • Turn the Virginia Eviction Notice Rules offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Virginia House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Virginia?
We buy Virginia houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What written notice must a Virginia landlord give before an eviction?

The notice depends on the reason, and a court will not enter an order of possession unless the landlord presents a proper termination notice and the court admits it into evidence. Rent problems, lease breaches, and the end of a month-to-month tenancy each follow different clocks.

SituationNotice periodCode section
Unpaid rent14 days after written notice to pay55.1-1245(F)
Breach that can be fixedLease ends no sooner than 30 days after receipt if not fixed in 21 days55.1-1245(A)
Breach that cannot be fixedNo sooner than 30 days after receipt55.1-1245(C)
Criminal or willful act threatening health or safetyImmediate termination and a possession case55.1-1245(C)
Week-to-week tenancy7 days before the next rent due date55.1-1253(A)
Month-to-month tenancy30 days before the next rent due date, unless the lease says otherwise55.1-1253(A)

How does the nonpayment notice work?

A landlord serves a written notice that the rent is unpaid and that the lease will end if it is not paid within 14 days. The landlord may terminate only if the tenant fails to pay within that period.

The same 14-day route applies when a rent check bounces or an electronic payment is rejected for insufficient funds. In that case the notice must say the rent must be paid by cash, cashier's check, certified check, or completed electronic funds transfer.

A change takes effect on July 1, 2027. From that date, a landlord who owns more than four rental units in Virginia, or more than a 10 percent interest in more than four, must first send a notice stating the exact amount owed if the debt is no more than one month's rent plus contracted late charges. The notice must offer a payment plan over the lesser of six months or the time left on the lease, and the landlord has to offer that plan only once during the lease term.

  • Before July 1, 2027: 14-day written notice, then possession under 55.1-1251.
  • From July 1, 2027: larger landlords add the exact-amount notice and payment plan offer.
  • Late fees stop accruing on the covered debt while the tenant keeps up with the plan.

What happens when a tenant breaks other lease terms?

For a breach the tenant can correct, the landlord serves a notice that names the acts and omissions and says the lease ends on a date at least 30 days after receipt if the breach is not remedied within 21 days. If the tenant fixes it before the date, the lease does not end.

If a tenant repeats a like breach after fixing the first one, the landlord may serve a notice that refers to the prior breach and ends the lease no sooner than 30 days after receipt, with no new cure period.

Serious conduct is different. Illegal drug activity involving a controlled substance, or another criminal or willful act that threatens health or safety, counts as an immediate nonremediable violation, even if the tenant did not personally act, since the tenant is presumed to know of activity by an authorized occupant, guest, or invitee unless the tenant proves otherwise. The landlord does not need to wait for a criminal conviction, and the court sets an initial hearing within 15 calendar days of service. A later hearing or trial follows within 30 calendar days of service.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Virginia house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What does the court process look like after notice?

The landlord files a sworn statement and gets a summons for unlawful detainer from a magistrate, clerk, or judge of the general district court. For residential tenancy cases the first hearing should occur within 21 days of filing, and no later than 30 days if the court cannot hear it sooner.

The summons must be served at least 10 days before the return day. The landlord may ask for all rent due as of the hearing date and may amend the figure if more comes due before the case ends. Rent is not prorated to the hearing date if the lease makes rent due on the first for the whole month and the landlord asks for the full month.

  • File the sworn statement and get the summons.
  • Serve the tenant at least 10 days before the return date.
  • Attend the first hearing within 21 days of filing, or 30 at the latest.
  • Present the termination notice and the lease; photocopies are allowed with an affidavit.

A judge who grants possession can order the writ of eviction to issue immediately if the landlord asks. The summons also carries a notice that employers may not punish a tenant for missing work to appear in court.

How long do the tenant's appeal and the sheriff's writ take?

The tenant has 10 days to appeal a general district court judgment to the circuit court, and the sheriff may not evict before that 10-day period ends. A tenant who appeals must post a bond and pay the writ tax within the same 10 days, although an indigent defendant does not have to post an appeal bond.

Once a writ issues, the sheriff must serve notice of intent to execute at least 72 hours before the eviction, including the date and time. A writ must be issued within 180 days of the possession judgment and is returnable within 30 days. If it is not executed in 30 days, it is vacated as a matter of law.

No writ issues if, after the possession judgment, the landlord signs a new written rental agreement with the tenant.

What about occupants who have no lease, or a former owner after foreclosure?

Virginia treats these cases differently. If an owner of a single-family home proves that no rental agreement ever existed, the occupant has no permission to be there, and the owner gave written notice to vacate at least 72 hours before filing, the court sets an emergency hearing within 14 days of filing, or 30 days at the outside.

If a former owner remains in a single-family home on the date of a foreclosure sale, that person becomes a tenant at sufferance. The new owner can end the tenancy with a written notice given at least three days before the effective date, then file for unlawful detainer. The former owner owes fair market rent from the sale date, plus damages, attorney fees, and court costs.

The squatters rights and adverse possession page on this site covers a separate legal question, so do not mix the two.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Virginia houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What does a landlord recover after the lease ends?

The landlord can seek possession and unpaid rent, plus actual damages, reasonable attorney fees, and service costs. Code 55.1-1251 does not allow a post-possession judgment for accelerated rent through the end of the term, and the landlord must mitigate damages.

A court may enter a judgment for money and possession at the same time without crediting the security deposit. After the tenant leaves, the deposit is credited under the Virginia deposit rules.

A tenant who stays after the lease ends without consent can be sued for possession and actual damages. A lease may include a liquidated damage amount of up to 150 percent of the daily rent for each day the tenant remains, and the limit is the plain daily rent for public or HUD-regulated housing.

How does an eviction notice affect selling the house?

If you are the landlord and you want to sell, you must still end or honor the tenancy through the legal steps above. Sending a notice does not by itself clear the house, and the sheriff, not the landlord, carries out a writ.

  • List your notice dates and the case number, if one exists.
  • Say whether the tenant pays, and how much is behind.
  • Photograph the property and gather the lease, receipts, and any damage records.

We buy houses as-is, including rentals with a tenant in place or vacant houses that need work. Share the facts and we will tell you what we can offer. For legal questions, such as the validity of a particular notice, speak with a Virginia landlord-tenant attorney or a legal aid office.

More questions about Virginia Eviction Notice Rules

How many days notice is required for unpaid rent in Virginia?

The landlord must give written notice and wait 14 days for payment before terminating the lease and seeking possession, under Code 55.1-1245(F).

How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy in Virginia?

Either side must give written notice at least 30 days before the next rent due date, unless the rental agreement sets a different period, under Code 55.1-1253.

Can a Virginia landlord evict immediately for criminal activity?

Yes, in limited cases. A criminal or willful act that threatens health or safety, including illegal drug activity, allows immediate termination and a possession case, and the landlord does not need to wait for a conviction.

How long does a tenant have to appeal an eviction judgment?

The tenant has 10 days to appeal to the circuit court, and the sheriff cannot evict before that period ends under Code 8.01-129.

How long is a writ of eviction valid in Virginia?

It must be issued within 180 days of the possession judgment and executed within 30 days of issuance, or it is vacated under Code 8.01-471.

When do the new payment plan rules take effect?

The payment plan rule for landlords with more than four rental units takes effect July 1, 2027, according to the version of Code 55.1-1245 published for that date.
